atoms.b:
The digital revolution

The digital revolution is the shift from ((analogue --digital)) technology to ((digital --analogue)) technology, which accelerated around the year ((2000 --1970)) as the internet became widely accessible and digital technologies became part of everyday life. Smartphones, social media, online banking, and ((remote --hard)) work are all examples of this shift.

atoms.a: Select the best definition of the digital revolution.
b: ++The shift from analogue to digital technology.
The replacement of computers by smartphones.
The improvement of agriculture through technology.

atoms.a: Which sentence best summarises the main idea of the text?
b: ++The digital revolution has transformed modern society through digital technology.
The internet has replaced all traditional technology.
The internet is the most important invention of the 20th century.

atoms.text: Not everyone benefits equally from the changes the digital revolution has brought. The digital divide refers to the gap between people who have access to digital technologies and those who do not.
atoms.sound: Not everyone benefits equally from the changes the digital revolution has brought. The digital divide refers to the gap between people who have access to digital technologies and those who do not.

atoms.text: Digital literacy is the ability to use digital technologies and media confidently and critically. It is one of the most important modern-day skills. However, people without reliable access to digital technology have fewer opportunities to develop this skill, putting them at a disadvantage in education, work, and everyday life.
